meta.description: Allow administrators to look up and update an existing user account's details in the CardDemo system's user security file.
meta.process_description: The program presents an administrator with a user update screen where they can enter a User ID to retrieve an existing user's profile (first name, last name, password, and user type) from the security file. Once the user record is displayed, the administrator can modify any of the editable fields and save the changes by pressing PF5, or navigate away using PF3/PF12 which also triggers a save attempt before returning to the previous screen. The program validates that all mandatory fields (User ID, First Name, Last Name, Password, User Type) are non-empty before writing changes, and only performs the file update if at least one field has actually been modified.

files.USRSEC: User security file storing all system user accounts including credentials and user type (Regular or Admin)

business_rules: User ID is mandatory and cannot be empty when looking up or updating a user account
First Name, Last Name, Password, and User Type are all mandatory fields and cannot be left blank when saving an update
A file update is only performed if at least one field (First Name, Last Name, Password, or User Type) has been changed from its current stored value — no unnecessary writes occur
If the entered User ID does not exist in the security file, the update is rejected with a 'User ID NOT found' error message
The record is read with an UPDATE lock (CICS READ UPDATE) to prevent concurrent modification of the same user record
PF3 saves any pending changes and returns the administrator to the calling program (defaulting to the Admin menu COADM01C if no calling program is recorded)
PF12 discards any unsaved changes and navigates directly back to the Admin menu (COADM01C) without saving
PF5 explicitly saves the updated user information while keeping the administrator on the update screen
PF4 clears the current screen input without saving
If the session communication area is empty (no prior context), the user is redirected to the sign-on screen (COSGN00C), preventing unauthorised direct access

variables.name: WS-VARIABLES
variables.description: Top-level working storage group holding all operational variables used by the User Update program (COUSR02C) during an administrator's session to look up and modify a user account.

variables.name: WS-PGMNAME
variables.description: The internal name of this program ('COUSR02C'), used when navigating between screens or logging activity, so the system knows which program is currently running the user update function.

variables.name: WS-TRANID
variables.description: The CICS transaction identifier ('CU02') assigned to the User Update function. This is the four-character code an administrator would use to invoke or re-invoke the user update screen directly from a CICS terminal.

variables.name: WS-MESSAGE
variables.description: The feedback message displayed to the administrator on the user update screen — for example, confirmation that a user record was successfully updated, or an error such as 'User ID NOT found' or 'mandatory field missing'.

variables.name: WS-USRSEC-FILE
variables.description: The name of the User Security File ('USRSEC') that stores all system user accounts, including credentials and roles. This value is used when issuing CICS file commands to read or update a user's account record.

variables.name: WS-ERR-FLG
variables.description: An error indicator that signals whether a validation problem has been detected during the update process. When set to 'Y', it stops the save operation and forces the screen to be redisplayed with an appropriate error message so the administrator can correct the input.

variables.name: ERR-FLG-ON
variables.description: Condition name meaning a validation error has been detected (e.g., a mandatory field is blank or the User ID does not exist). When true, the update is halted and the administrator is shown an error message on screen.

variables.name: ERR-FLG-OFF
variables.description: Condition name meaning no validation errors have been detected. When true, the program may proceed normally with reading or saving the user account record.

variables.name: WS-RESP-CD
variables.description: The response code returned by CICS after a file operation (such as reading or updating the User Security File). A non-zero value indicates a problem — for example, a record not found or a file I/O error — which the program uses to decide whether to show an error to the administrator.

variables.name: WS-REAS-CD
variables.description: The reason code accompanying the CICS response code, providing additional detail about why a file operation failed (e.g., record locked by another user, or end of file). Used alongside WS-RESP-CD to diagnose and handle file access issues during user account updates.

variables.name: WS-USR-MODIFIED
variables.description: A flag that tracks whether the administrator has actually changed at least one field on the user account (First Name, Last Name, Password, or User Type). If no changes were made, the file update is skipped entirely, preventing unnecessary writes to the User Security File.

variables.name: USR-MODIFIED-YES
variables.description: Condition name indicating that the administrator has changed at least one field on the user account. When true, the program proceeds to write the updated record back to the User Security File.

variables.name: USR-MODIFIED-NO
variables.description: Condition name indicating that the administrator has not changed any fields on the user account. When true, the file update is bypassed to avoid an unnecessary write to the User Security File.

variables.name: CDEMO-CU02-INFO
variables.description: A group of fields that carry context information for the User Update function — specifically, which user was selected from the user list screen and pagination state. This data is passed between screens to maintain continuity during the administrator's session.

variables.name: CDEMO-CU02-USRID-FIRST
variables.description: The User ID of the first user account displayed on the current page of the user list. Used for pagination purposes so the system knows where the current page of results begins when the administrator navigates back to the user list.

variables.name: CDEMO-CU02-USRID-LAST
variables.description: The User ID of the last user account displayed on the current page of the user list. Used for pagination so the system knows where the current page of results ends when navigating forward or backward through the user list.

variables.name: CDEMO-CU02-PAGE-NUM
variables.description: The current page number within the user list that the administrator was viewing before selecting a user to edit. Retained so the administrator can be returned to the correct page of the user list after completing the update.

variables.name: CDEMO-CU02-NEXT-PAGE-FLG
variables.description: A flag indicating whether there are more user accounts available beyond the current page of the user list. Helps the user list screen determine whether to enable or disable the 'next page' navigation option.

variables.name: NEXT-PAGE-YES
variables.description: Condition name indicating that additional pages of user accounts exist beyond the current page. When true, the user list screen allows the administrator to navigate forward to see more users.

variables.name: NEXT-PAGE-NO
variables.description: Condition name indicating that the current page is the last page of user accounts — no further records exist. When true, the user list screen disables forward navigation.

variables.name: CDEMO-CU02-USR-SEL-FLG
variables.description: A flag indicating whether the administrator has selected a specific user from the user list to edit. Used to determine whether the update screen should be pre-populated with an existing user's details.

variables.name: CDEMO-CU02-USR-SELECTED
variables.description: The User ID passed from the user list screen (COUSR00C) that identifies which specific user account the administrator wants to look up and edit. This is the key used to retrieve the user's record from the User Security File.

variables.name: DFHCOMMAREA
variables.description: The CICS communication area passed between programs and transactions. It carries session context — such as which user is logged in, which program called this one, and which user account is being edited — allowing the User Update program to maintain state across screen interactions.

variables.name: LK-COMMAREA
variables.description: The raw communication area data passed into this program from the previous CICS transaction or program. Its length is checked at program entry: if it is empty (no prior context), the administrator is redirected to the sign-on screen to prevent unauthorised direct access to the user update function.

paragraphs.name: MAIN-PARA
paragraphs.description: MAIN-PARA is the central orchestration paragraph that controls the entire user update session flow. It determines whether an administrator is starting a new session or continuing an existing one, then routes their key presses to the appropriate business actions such as saving changes, clearing the screen, or navigating away.

paragraphs.name: PROCESS-ENTER-KEY
paragraphs.description: This paragraph handles the administrator's request to look up a user account by User ID. It validates that a User ID has been entered, retrieves the matching user profile from the security file, and displays the editable account details on screen for the administrator to review and modify.

paragraphs.name: UPDATE-USER-INFO
paragraphs.description: This paragraph validates all mandatory fields on the user update screen, then compares the administrator's submitted changes against the current stored profile to determine whether any fields were actually modified before committing the update to the security file. It enforces data integrity by rejecting blank fields and avoiding unnecessary file writes when nothing has changed.

paragraphs.name: RETURN-TO-PREV-SCREEN
paragraphs.description: This paragraph handles the navigation away from the user update screen, returning the administrator to the appropriate previous screen. It ensures the session context is correctly stamped with the originating transaction before handing control to the destination screen.

paragraphs.name: SEND-USRUPD-SCREEN
paragraphs.description: Prepares and displays the User Update screen to the administrator, showing current user account details along with any validation or status messages resulting from the most recent action.

paragraphs.name: RECEIVE-USRUPD-SCREEN
paragraphs.description: Captures the administrator's input from the user update screen, reading all field values the administrator has entered or modified (such as first name, last name, password, and user type) so the program can proceed with validation and saving changes to the user account.

paragraphs.name: POPULATE-HEADER-INFO
paragraphs.description: Populates the standard header section of the User Update screen with current date, time, application titles, and transaction identifiers, ensuring the administrator always sees accurate context information at the top of the screen before any user data is displayed or edited.

paragraphs.name: READ-USER-SEC-FILE
paragraphs.description: This paragraph retrieves an existing user's account record from the security file with an exclusive update lock, preventing other processes from modifying the same record simultaneously. Based on the outcome, it either displays the user's current details ready for editing, or presents the administrator with an appropriate error message if the user cannot be found or the file is unavailable.

paragraphs.name: UPDATE-USER-SEC-FILE
paragraphs.description: This paragraph commits the administrator's changes to the user security file by permanently writing the updated user profile record. It then informs the administrator of the outcome — success, user not found, or a system error — and refreshes the update screen accordingly.

paragraphs.name: CLEAR-CURRENT-SCREEN
paragraphs.description: Resets the user update screen to a blank state, discarding any data currently displayed without saving changes. This allows the administrator to start fresh when editing a user account, clearing all previously entered or retrieved field values from the screen.

paragraphs.name: INITIALIZE-ALL-FIELDS
paragraphs.description: Resets the user update screen to a blank state, clearing all previously displayed user profile data and any status messages. This prepares a clean slate for the administrator to enter a new User ID lookup or begin a fresh update session.
